b. ἰλλόμενος χαλκή〈ισιν〉: Hesiod says (Theog. 521 ff.) that Prometheus was bound and that the eagle was sent against him because of the theft of fire; but Duris (76 FGrH 47 J.) says it was because he loved Athena, and that therefore the inhabitants of the Caucasus region sacrifice to Zeus and Athena alone, because they were responsible for Prometheus' punishment, but they honor Heracles exceedingly in gratitude for his shooting of the eagle. So Apollonius, having come to the Caucasus, naturally mentioned these things.
12 Apoll. Bibl. II 119 Acusil. 2 FGrH 13 J.

1251-53. τὸν μὲν ἐπ’ ἀκροτ〈άτης〉: In the evening, they say, the chiefs saw the eagle upon Prometheus 〈...〉. παραιθύξας δέ, having blown past, that is, having made a breeze, with the force of its wings it shook the sails.
24 lacuna indicated by W
1254. 〈αἰθερίοιο:〉 instead of 'air-traversing'. Lm
1255. ἶσα δ’ ἐυξέστοις: The feathers on its wings were equal to well-polished oars, that is, to rowing oars.
1256. δηρὸν δ’ οὐ μετέπειτα: The word order must be reversed: 'and afterwards not after a long time'. LmP
1260 a. 〈Ἄργοιο:〉 of the son of Phrixus. Lm
b. δαημοσύνηισιν: by knowledge of the places. Lm (P)
6 δαη- in the words of the poet G. d'Arnaud Lect. graec. 1730, 240
1269. 〈τοῖο θεοῦ:〉 of Ares. Sm
1270. 〈πεπτάμενον:〉 Herodian (I 471, 10 L.) with acute accent on the penult. Lg
1272. μελισταγέας: sweet, pleasant. Lg (P)

1273. ἐνναέταις τε θεοῖς: to the local gods; for it was customary for those residing in a foreign land to sacrifice to the local gods and heroes. They say that Alexander the Macedonian also did this in Ilium.
13 Strab. XIII 593 Arr. Anab. I 11, 7
1275. καὶ νηὸς ἐναίσιμα: the proper things, that is, for good omens and acceptable.
15 εὐπρόσδεκτα Fr. : -οσδέκτοις
1279-80. εἴτ’ οὖν μειλιχίῃ: whether by approaching Aeetes gently we should test him, or in some other way. ἐπήβολος means 'secure'; thus Amerias also rendered it in his Glosses.
18 Ἀμερίας in P : ἀπαμερίας in L : ἀπ’ Ἀμερίας in H
1281. παρηγορίηισιν: by encouragements and counsels. Lg (P)
20 scholion a is placed after b in L
1282 a. ὑψόθι νη’ ἐκέλ〈ευσεν〉: in the depth of the river, not having moored to the land. Homer (Ξ 77): 'we will moor high on the anchor-cables'.
b. ἐπ’ εὐναίηισιν ἐρύσσαι: to drag upon the anchors, to moor with the anchors.
